stem: In the American Stroke Association B.E. F.A.S.T. stroke-warning mnemonic, what does the letter T mean?
rationale: The American Stroke Association's current B.E. F.A.S.T. mnemonic identifies Balance loss, Eye or vision changes, Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call 911. Stroke is an emergency, and emergency services should be activated immediately when warning signs occur, even if symptoms later resolve.
educational_objective: Recall that T in B.E. F.A.S.T. means Time to call 911 and recognize stroke symptoms as an emergency.
source_organization: American Stroke Association / American Heart Association
source_document_title: Stroke Symptoms and Warning Signs; B.E. F.A.S.T. Experience
source_locator: B.E. F.A.S.T. mnemonic > T = Time to Call 911
source_claim_supported: In B.E. F.A.S.T., T means Time to call 911; suspected stroke requires immediate emergency action.
correction_summary: Updated the stem to the American Stroke Association's current B.E. F.A.S.T. wording while preserving the validated T component. Removed explanatory cueing from distractors.
audit_findings: C exactly matches the current American Stroke Association mnemonic. A, B, and D are not B.E. F.A.S.T. components. No second answer remains.
